nodes.label: Need
nodes.text: A state of felt deprivation.
nodes.sub: A patient with chest pain needs a diagnosis.
nodes.src: A need is a state of felt deprivation. People need food, safety and health.

nodes.label: Want
nodes.text: The form a need takes, shaped by culture and personal experience.
nodes.sub: A particular cardiologist or a scan at a well-known centre.
nodes.src: A want is the form a need takes, shaped by culture and personal experience.

nodes.label: Demand
nodes.text: A want backed by the ability and willingness to pay.
nodes.sub: Many Egyptians want a full annual check-up; only some can pay for one.
nodes.src: A demand is a want backed by the ability and willingness to pay. Many Egyptians want a full annual check-up. Only some can pay for one

caption.text: In health care, needs are often defined by professionals; wants and demands come from patients.
caption.src: Needs in health care are therefore often defined by professionals, while wants and demands come from patients

nodes.label: What the customer gains
nodes.text: The benefits of the service.
nodes.src: The gains are the benefits of the service.

nodes.label: What the customer gives up
nodes.text: Money, time, travel and anxiety.
nodes.src: The costs include money, time, travel and anxiety.

nodes.label: Customer value
nodes.text: The difference between what a customer gains and what the customer gives up.
nodes.src: Customer value is the difference between what a customer gains and what the customer gives up.

caption.text: A patient who waits three hours for a routine test has paid a high cost, even if the fee was low.
caption.src: A patient who waits three hours for a routine test has paid a high cost, even if the fee was low.

caption.text: **Satisfaction** is the patient's judgement of whether the service met expectations: it depends on both performance and expectation.
caption.src: Satisfaction is the patient's judgement of whether the service met expectations. It depends on both performance and expectation.

slides.title: Quality in health care has two sides

nodes.label: Technical quality
nodes.text: Whether the result is correct.
nodes.sub: An accurate haemoglobin, a clear image.
nodes.src: Technical quality is whether the result is correct: an accurate haemoglobin, a clear image.

nodes.label: Functional quality
nodes.text: How the service was delivered.
nodes.src: Functional quality is how the service was delivered: courtesy, cleanliness, explanation.

caption.text: Patients usually cannot judge technical quality, so they judge what they can see.
caption.src: Patients usually cannot judge technical quality, so they judge what they can see

nodes.label: Transaction
nodes.text: A single exchange.
nodes.sub: A patient pays for one lipid profile and leaves.
nodes.src: A single exchange is a transaction. A patient pays for one lipid profile and leaves.

nodes.label: Relationship
nodes.text: Long-term, trusting links: relationship marketing.
nodes.sub: A diabetic patient may need a glycated haemoglobin test every three months for life.
nodes.src: A diabetic patient may need a glycated haemoglobin test every three months for life. The laboratory that earns this patient's trust gains a long relationship. Relationship marketing is the practice of building such long-term, trusting links.

caption.text: An **exchange** is the act of obtaining something of value by offering something in return.
caption.src: An exchange is the act of obtaining something of value by offering something in return.

nodes.label: Patients who walk in
nodes.text: Actual and potential buyers.
nodes.src: A market is the set of actual and potential buyers of a product. For a laboratory, the market includes patients who walk in

nodes.label: Doctors who refer them
nodes.text: Each group has different needs.
nodes.src: doctors who refer them, clinics that send samples and insurers that pay. Each group has different needs

nodes.label: Clinics that send samples
nodes.text: Each group has different needs.
nodes.src: clinics that send samples and insurers that pay. Each group has different needs

nodes.label: Insurers that pay
nodes.text: A good service plans for all of them.
nodes.src: insurers that pay. Each group has different needs, and a good service plans for all of them.

caption.text: A **product** is anything offered to satisfy a need or want: a good (a glucose meter) or a service (a blood test). Most health care is a service, or a service wrapped around a good.
caption.src: A product is anything offered to satisfy a need or want. It can be a physical good, such as a glucose meter. It can be a service, such as a blood test. Most health care is a service, or a service wrapped around a good.

nodes.label: Creating awareness
nodes.text: A new mammography unit must tell women it is open.
nodes.src: Creating awareness. People cannot use a service they do not know exists. A new mammography unit must tell women and their doctors that it is open

nodes.label: Studying what customers want
nodes.text: Survey referring doctors about turnaround times.
nodes.src: Studying what customers want. Marketing research finds out what patients and doctors need. A laboratory might survey referring doctors about turnaround times

nodes.label: Product planning
nodes.text: From the first idea to launch.
nodes.src: Product planning. A product is a bundle of benefits. Planning runs from the first idea to launch.

nodes.label: After-sales service
nodes.text: Everything after the result is issued.
nodes.src: After-sales service. In health care this means everything after the result is issued.

nodes.label: Pricing
nodes.text: The amount of money charged.
nodes.src: Pricing. Price is the amount of money charged for a product.

nodes.label: Distribution
nodes.text: Branches, collection points, home visits.
nodes.src: Distribution. This is how the service reaches people: branches, collection points, home visits, mobile units.

nodes.label: Selling
nodes.text: Most selling is really informing.
nodes.src: Selling. Selling is supplying goods and services to target customers, directly or through others. In health care, most selling is really informing.

nodes.label: Packaging and presentation
nodes.text: A clean reception and clear signs.
nodes.src: Packaging and presentation. For goods, packaging protects the product and carries information. For services, the equivalent is the setting: a clean reception, clear signs and a well-designed report.

nodes.label: Advertising
nodes.text: The most restricted tool in health care.
nodes.src: Advertising. Advertising makes a service known to a wide audience. In health care it is the most restricted tool

nodes.label: Collecting feedback
nodes.text: A short survey after a scan.
nodes.src: Collecting feedback. Feedback shows whether patients were satisfied and what to improve. A short survey after a scan costs little

nodes.label: The customer cannot judge quality well
nodes.text: **Information asymmetry**: a gap in knowledge that gives the provider power.
nodes.src: The customer cannot judge quality well. Most patients cannot tell whether a test was performed correctly. This gap in knowledge is called information asymmetry. It gives the provider power

nodes.label: The decider, the payer and the user may differ
nodes.text: A doctor orders a scan, an insurer may pay, and the patient undergoes it.
nodes.src: The decider, the payer and the user may differ. A doctor orders a scan, an insurer may pay, and the patient undergoes it.

nodes.label: Demand can be created by the provider
nodes.text: **Supplier-induced demand**: a provider who both advises and sells can recommend more than is needed.
nodes.src: Demand can be created by the provider. A provider who both advises and sells can recommend more than is needed. Economists call this supplier-induced demand.

nodes.label: Stakes are high
nodes.text: A misleading advertisement for a test can lead to missed disease or needless anxiety.
nodes.src: Stakes are high. A misleading advertisement for shampoo wastes money. A misleading advertisement for a test can lead to missed disease or needless anxiety.

nodes.label: Society has an interest
nodes.text: Society sets rules on what may be promised and how.
nodes.src: Society has an interest. Health care is partly funded by public money and affects public health. Society therefore sets rules on what may be promised and how.

caption.src: It gives the provider power, and with power comes responsibility.

nodes.label: Production
nodes.text: Customers want what is cheap and available.
nodes.src: A production orientation assumes customers want what is cheap and available. The focus is efficiency.

nodes.label: Product
nodes.text: Customers want the highest quality.
nodes.src: A product orientation assumes customers want the highest quality. The focus is technical excellence

nodes.label: Selling
nodes.text: Customers will not buy enough unless pushed.
nodes.src: A selling orientation assumes customers will not buy enough unless pushed. In health care this leads directly to the ethical problems

nodes.label: Marketing
nodes.text: Starts from the customer's needs.
nodes.src: A marketing orientation starts from the customer's needs and builds the service around them.

nodes.label: Societal marketing
nodes.text: Adds the long-term interest of society.
nodes.sub: The most appropriate for health services.
nodes.src: A societal marketing orientation adds the long-term interest of society. For health services, the last is the most appropriate.

caption.text: A service must meet patients' needs, cover its costs and protect public health together.
caption.src: A service must meet patients' needs, cover its costs and protect public health together.
